read_from: The route text as served: field 1 (the route text) of each row of reader/data/route-store of the main branch at commit 306f3b285898, store_version 87b13b1169b4 (its index.json), for "DBnary English Wiktionary source-explicit Hebrew translations and English glosses" (M37): 6,156 routes (axis: routes), 5,166 letters keys (axis: keys). The definition field of the same row equals the route text on 7 of the routes. The source audit (builder/02-audit.mjs, evidence about the source and no part of any test): the source is DBnary's extract of the English Wiktionary, en_dbnary_ontolex.ttl.bz2 in ledgers/work/ldmprs/source-cache/dbnary-english-2026-07-15/, and the lane's own rule for it reads: "DBnary source-explicit targetLanguage heb translation writtenForm joined only to its source-explicit English gloss resource and exact English lexical-entry rdfs:label". Each of the 6,604 records in the dictionary store names its subject, which carries the page title, the part of speech and the number of the translation; the page title equals the record's English on all 6,604, and all 6,156 routes are tied to a record with the same English, the same gloss in the definition field and a Hebrew headword of the same letters. So a route comes from one field, the title of one English page, under one translation table's gloss, and no test here stands on a guess about a field. No key to the signs is on file. In the small files of the source cache (dbnary-license.html, source-manifest-v1.json, dbnary-hebrew-translation-gloss-manifest-v1.json, source-headers.txt), searched with word ends round the words and without them, every line that holds the name of a sign is the lane's own: its rule for the Hebrew keys, its name for a class of forms, or the id of a sample row that carries the section name Suffix; none says how the source uses a sign. The works-own-stamp folder speaks of this source's release and says its archive's prologue holds only Turtle prefixes, and the archive was not unpacked for this (builder/05-key-search.mjs, source-audit/key-search.json). The nearest thing on file to an account of a sign is the source's own section name on each page, which files every row with a hyphen at its end under Prefix and every row with a hyphen at its start under Suffix (builder/figures.mjs stops if not). Wiktionary's own guides to writing an entry are not on file, and fetching them needs the owner's word and was not done. So every shape's meaning here begins "unverified:".

definitions.terms: In every test a character is one Unicode code point (every route that holds a mark here holds only characters of 16 bits, so a code point is one index of the JavaScript string). A letter is any character of Unicode category L (JavaScript \p{L}), of any script and in either case. No test asks for a digit, for whitespace, or for uppercase or lowercase as a class. Nothing is trimmed: the text is the whole route text as it stands, which is the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def; the text before and the text after the mark are the template's c.before and c.after. Empty means that the named text has no character at all, as at the start or the end of the route. Directly before and directly after name the one character next to the mark or next to the named string; where the mark or the string stands at that end of the text no character stands there, so a test that asks for a character there fails, and a test that says if there is one passes. The whole text, exactly, means that the text equals the named string character for character. The word round the mark means three runs put together, with nothing between them: the run of letters that ends directly before the mark, taken back to the first character that is not a letter or to the start of the text; the mark itself; and the run of letters that begins directly after the mark, taken on to the first character that is not a letter or to the end of the text; either run of letters may be empty. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it, and a full stop after » belongs to the sentence and not to the string. The apostrophe in every string is the straight one, U+0027, and the é in the string d'état is the one character U+00E9. Every string and every list minds case and is matched exact to the character, so «s» is the lowercase letter. No test uses the words begins with or contains.
definitions.first_match: For each mark the shapes are tried in the order they stand in this file; the first whose test holds names the occurrence, and no later shape is tried for it. A shape's container field is not part of its test: no test here looks at the container, and the checker compares the field afterwards. An occurrence that no shape of its mark takes makes the classifier throw, and none does: no shape here is a catch-all.

homonyms.reason: The route text carries no entry number, and the source has no entry for the Hebrew at all: a Hebrew word stands here only as a translation on an English page, so nothing in this source says that two Hebrew words of one spelling are two words. The store's record keeps the Hebrew as written (headwords), and 3,977 of its 6,604 records write it with no point or accent (a maqaf is neither), so even the written form cannot tell them apart. The id the source does carry is the English page, its part of speech and the number of the translation (the record's loc), which names the translation and not a Hebrew entry. A letters key's texts are the English pages that give that spelling. Of the 789 keys with more than one text (axis: keys, the store's own keys, on which a geresh or a maqaf makes another key), the records write 459 one way and 330 in two or more ways (example key חברה: 5 texts, 3 written forms).

branches.question: Some rows hold only the beginning or the ending of a word, with a hyphen on the side where the rest would go: mega-. Such a piece cannot stand alone in a verse. In this dictionary each of these rows is the title of a page about that word part, and the Hebrew is what that page gives as its translation. Should the page print these rows as readings? They print as they do today until you rule. To leave them out the page needs one step of its own, because a declaration cannot leave a row out.

options.means: The page prints each row as one reading, as written, as it does today: mega-.
The page prints no pill for these rows, once it has the one step of its own that this answer needs; until then they print as they do today. They stay in the store as they are.

not_done_here: This ledger leaves to the store every route that holds no mark, because a shape stands only at a mark, and every question of whether a row renders the word it is filed under; the 7 rows it names for this stand in rows-for-the-store-v1.jsonl, outside the shapes, as examples and no census, and nothing is struck. It leaves to the page the step that the answer no_pill asks for, since a declaration can cut a row and has no field that leaves a whole row out.
